summary: RFC 5586 generalized the pseudowire Associated Channel Header into the Generic Associated Channel, but its registries were spread across unrelated places. This document gathers them into a new Generic Associated Channel registry.

eli5.summary: Lists of numbers were scattered in many drawers. This puts them in one drawer.

questions: what is the g-ach parameters registry
what is the generic associated channel
why did iana move the g-ach registries
subtitle: IANA gathers the scattered Generic Associated Channel registries into one place under the MPLS heading.

tldr.problem: After RFC 5586 turned the pseudowire Associated Channel Header into the Generic Associated Channel (G-ACh), its registries and allocations ended up spread across different, sometimes unrelated, registries.
tldr.mechanism: IANA creates one new Generic Associated Channel (G-ACh) Parameters registry under the MPLS Architecture heading, renames the Pseudowire Associated Channel Types registry, and moves the related registries into it unchanged.
tldr.outcome: There is a single view of all G-ACh registries, which simplifies future assignments and avoids conflicts.

today: RFC 7214 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It updates RFC 5586, RFC 6374, RFC 6378, RFC 6427 and RFC 6428.

sections.title: Why the Registries Move
sections.content:
RFC 5586 generalized the pseudowire Associated Channel Header (PW-ACH) into the Generic Associated Channel (G-ACh). Registries and allocations for G-ACh namespaces had nonetheless been distributed across different registries.

RFC 7214 coalesces them into a new registry in the Multiprotocol Label Switching Architecture (MPLS) name space. The stated purposes are to place the G-ACh registries in their natural home and to give a single view that simplifies future assignments and avoids potential conflicts.
sections.eli5: Many lists of numbers were stored in different places. The goal is to keep them together where people would look for them.

sections.title: The New Parameters Registry
sections.content:
IANA has created a new Generic Associated Channel (G-ACh) Parameters registry. It is the common registry that holds every registry moved by the document.

Moved registries are replaced with pointers to the new URL or with a redirect, and IANA has added RFC 7214 as a reference for every registry that was moved or renamed.
sections.eli5: There is now one big cabinet for all the related lists. The old drawers have signs that point to the cabinet.

sections.title: Renaming the Associated Channel Types Registry
sections.content:
The "Pseudowire Associated Channel Types" registry is renamed to "MPLS Generalized Associated Channel (G-ACh) Types (including Pseudowire Associated Channel Types)" to make its generalized status explicit. It is moved into the new parameters registry because any additional registries depend on the Associated Channel Header Type.

When it was moved, these RFCs had G-ACh Types allocated: RFC 4385, RFC 5586, RFC 5718, RFC 5885, RFC 6374, RFC 6378, RFC 6426, RFC 6427, RFC 6428, RFC 6435, RFC 6478 and RFC 6671.
sections.eli5: The main list got a longer, clearer name so people know it covers more than just one kind of thing.

sections.title: Consolidating the Related Registries
sections.content:
Registries are pulled from three places. From the PWE Parameters registry come the G-ACh Types and the CC/CV MEP-ID TLV registry. From the MPLS LSP Ping Parameters registry come the Measurement Timestamp Type, the Loss/Delay Measurement Control Code query codes and response codes, and the MPLS Loss/Delay Measurement TLV Object. From the MPLS OAM Parameters registry come the Fault OAM Message Type, Flag and TLV registries, and the PSC Request and PSC TLV registries.

Because all sub-registries of the MPLS OAM Parameters registry were removed, IANA has removed that registry as well.
sections.eli5: Lists were collected from three different places and put in the new cabinet. The empty old drawer was then taken away.

sections.title: Which RFCs Are Updated
sections.content:
RFC 7214 updates RFC 5586 by renaming the Pseudowire Associated Channel Types registry. It also updates RFC 6374, RFC 6378, RFC 6427 and RFC 6428, because their G-ACh registries now live in the common one.

All the registries are moved without any change to their content. The only reason to move them is to create one place where all G-ACh parameters can be found.
sections.eli5: Only the addresses of the lists changed, not what is written on them.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The IANA instructions in this document do not directly introduce any new security issues. The registries are moved unchanged, so no values or meanings change.
sections.eli5: Moving lists around does not make anything less safe.
